title: Feedback subtraction reduces the 2001-2022 DOISST step effect by 72-74% but increases the OI v2 step effect in five linear models
abstract: We tested how known SST input steps change a trend budget after an interannual feedback response is removed. We used published SST and radiation response series from five linear atmosphere models, with no changing external forcing. For 2001-2022, the two DOISST corrections give raw-minus-corrected radiation-trend effects of -0.101 and -0.109 W m-2 per decade. After feedback subtraction, their effects are -0.0275 and -0.0281, a reduction of 72.8% and 74.3%. Conditional block intervals include zero. The OI v2 June 2018 correction instead gives a direct effect of -0.0113 and a residual effect of -0.0314, an increase by a factor of 2.78. Its three-year block interval is -0.0528 to -0.0083. The 2010-2022 OI v2 effect is -0.0703. An exact budget separates the radiation, warming and feedback terms. A correction-amplitude test and independent numerical audit support inspection. The residual is apparent forcing, not observed forcing. The test fixes published corrections, omits later OI v2 events, and uses mask SST rather than global air temperature. It does not test an observed forcing estimate.

display.caption: Direct radiation-trend effects and apparent-forcing effects after feedback subtraction, from the same raw and corrected SST records.
Apparent forcing after zero to twice the published step correction. The model records contain no changing external forcing.
